Classify each 3x3 self-analysis of a chess move. You give FOUR independent
verdicts per note: one for each Why answer. The answers DO NOT rescue each
other — judge every answer on its own words.

A 3x3 self-analysis answers four questions:
  Why1 — "Why did I choose that move?"
  Why2 — "Why is my move not ideal?"
  Why3 — "Why is the better move better than my chosen move?"
  Why4 — "What do I do in the future so this doesn't happen again?"

Judge Why1, Why2, Why3 as INTENT (one of SPECIFIC, GENERIC, BLANK).
Judge Why4 as LESSON (one of REAL, FILLER, BLANK).

Do NOT let one answer change the verdict for another. A specific Why1 does
not make a filler Lesson real. A real Lesson does not make a generic Why1
specific. Each answer is scored on its own text.

INTENT (for Why1, Why2, Why3)
=============================
SPECIFIC — Names something concrete about the position, the move, or the
  player's own thinking. "Concrete" means: a piece, a square, a plan, a
  tactic, a mental process, a misread, or an intent tied to this position.
  Short is fine. Overlap with another answer is fine. Repeating a point
  in different words is fine.
  Examples:
    "Clearing the e-file for my rook."
    "To stop ...Bb4 before I castled."
    "Doubling rooks before opening the c-file."
    "It left my f2 pawn without a defender."
    "The other move wins the h-pawn because their rook is overloaded."
GENERIC — Could fit almost any move at almost any point in any game.
  No piece, square, plan, or intent you could point to.
  Examples:
    "Just a good-looking move."
    "Trying to improve my position."
    "Developing."
    "It was a mistake."
    "The other move was stronger."
BLANK — No text, whitespace only, or `(blank)`.

LESSON (for Why4)
=================
When in doubt, choose REAL. FILLER is reserved for text that names NOTHING
you could watch for next time.

REAL — Names something identifiable to watch for next game: a pattern, a
  piece, a square, a mental habit, a method step, or a checklist item.
  Short counts. Repeated across many moments counts (seeing "look at
  checks" on ten moments is useful information, not a defect). Prescriptive
  phrasing counts. Negative lessons count. Any takeaway that you could
  sincerely use as a to-do item on your next move is REAL.
  Examples:
    "Count attackers and defenders on every capture square."
    "When attacked, list every retreat and every counter-attack."
    "Watch for discovered attacks when my queen moves."
    "Before every move, ask what my opponent's last move threatens."
    "Sit on my hands for ten seconds and recheck the board."
FILLER — Names nothing you could watch for. Vague encouragement, defeatist
  remarks, "I don't know" shrugs, or restated outcomes. If a reasonable
  reader could not derive a single checklist item from it, it is FILLER.
  Examples:
    "Try harder."
    "Just play better chess."
    "Bad day at the board."
    "Who knows."
BLANK — No text, whitespace only, or `(blank)`.

Output format
=============
Return the verdict list FIRST, before any explanation. Preferably return
ONLY the verdict list.
One line per note, exactly this shape (keep ordering WHY1 → WHY2 → WHY3 → LESSON):

<index>: WHY1=<SPECIFIC|GENERIC|BLANK> WHY2=<SPECIFIC|GENERIC|BLANK> WHY3=<SPECIFIC|GENERIC|BLANK> LESSON=<REAL|FILLER|BLANK>

Notes to classify follow, one block per index.

0:
  Why1: I wanted to activate my rook by opening the d-file.
  Why2: It dropped a pawn to the bishop fork on b5.
  Why3: Nf6 maintains the knight and prevents the fork.
  Why4: Look for piece forks before advancing pawns.
1:
  Why1: I thought it was a good move.
  Why2: My rook was undefended after the move.
  Why3: Rd1 defends the rook and keeps pressure.
  Why4: Be more careful.
2:
  Why1: (blank)
  Why2: The move allowed a discovered attack on the queen.
  Why3: Ke2 sidesteps the discovered attack and keeps the king safe.
  Why4: (blank)
